newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to pay pensioners with bonds, cash - report.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to pay pensioners with bonds, cash - report.

text.p: Argentina's government is going to pay up to half its $800 million debt in backdated pension payments with bonds and the rest in cash, Clarin newspaper reported Tuesday.
As much as half the debt will be paid by giving Bocon Previsional bonds to the pensioners said Clarin, quoting Social Security Secretary Carlos Torres.
The bond payments will start this year while the remaining cash payments will be phased in next year and in 1999. The full amount will be paid by 1999.
The Bocon bonds to be paid will be series one and two and pensioners will have the option of whether they receive bonds denominated in dollars or pesos.

The payments are the result of a Supreme Court ruling in December that pension payments be adjusted in line with the cost of living. The case was brought by 70,000 pensioners, and the court ruled that a 13.8 percent increase was due on state pensions for the period from 1991 to 1994.
Officials had previously stated the government was considering issuing a new bond to cover the payments, but paying the debt with outstanding bonds had also been an option.
